svg.title: When both pulses are centered at x, use cutoffindependence and homogeneity instead of mul- tiplying distributions at their common pole. Two cutoffs equal to one near x have a difference supported away from x; source-free integration by parts makes their fluxes equal. Replace the cutoffby its dilation by a factor two about x. A jet-order-j pulse scales by 2−4−j; the other scales by 2−4−l; the volume and cutoffderivative together contribute 23, and a motion homogeneous of degree e = 0 or 1 contributes 2e. Thus the common flux Z equals 2e−5−j−lZ. That coefficient is strictly smaller than one, so Z = 0. When neither pulse is centered at x, their fields are smooth throughout the support of the cutoff, and the source-free divergence identity gives zero. When precisely one pulse is centered there and the other is at a spectator point, (FS2) gives minus the covariance with the transformed distinguished leg.
